text: Version 5 is issued with status Draft and no approval recorded, although the lifecycle gate expects an approved BRD before the PRD.
why: This run is the D-RCV-60 realignment: no human approval step is available and the run must not stop for one.
read: The document is complete and may be used to derive the PRDs; the approval table is filled by the Product Owner and the business owner afterwards.
applied_in: section 12.2 and the closing paragraph of section 12
impact: The PRD work starts from a Draft BRD; the status changes when the approval is recorded.

text: The business epics EP01 to EP08 used by the realignment wave map are read as E1 to E8 of the release plan, in order.
why: The wave map fixes the wave of EP01 to EP08, section 8 fixes the release and theme of E1 to E8, and no source states the correspondence.
read: EP01 is Epic 1 and its 30 Nov 2026 release, EP02 is Epic 2 and 31 Dec 2026, and so on to EP08 and 30 Jun 2027.
impact: If the codes do not correspond in order, the business epic column of the trace table and the wave of every story change.

text: The constraint Built on ACE is read as 19 services inside one ACE platform, not as one service.
why: D-RCV-60 adopts Architecture v5, and ADR-013 supersedes the single-service decision ADR-002.
read: The Workbench stays inside ACE: one AKS cluster, one database, one front end and one set of ACE shared services, with 19 services inside it.
impact: A reader who takes the version 4 wording would size one deployable instead of 19.

text: The constraint Modular monolith is read as one schema and login per service inside the single ACE database.
why: D-RCV-60 and ADR-014 give every service its own schema and login; ADR-021 gives each service its own migration sequence.
read: There is no database per service and no shared recovery schema; the module boundaries are still checked at build time.
impact: The physical schema and the database stories follow the per-service split.

text: The constraint Programmatic workflow with no Temporal is read as superseded by the reusable Temporal layer.
why: D-RCV-60 and ADR-016 replace the shared scheduler with Temporal Schedules and move a case by a durable workflow; the Temporal and Drools design fixes one parent case workflow with a child workflow per stage.
read: Case, stage and task state is still held in the owner's database and still described in CMMN 1.1 terms; what changes is the engine that moves it and the clock.
impact: Sizing and the non-functional targets for timers follow the workflow platform, not the old programmatic loop.

text: The four owner cells in section 9 that name persons are replaced by the value placeholder, and the role behind each is left to be confirmed.
why: The run forbids person names in any output, and the source does not record the role of those persons separately.
read: DL06, DL12 and DL13 carry the placeholder as the whole owner cell; DL20 keeps the solution architect and carries the placeholder for the second owner.
impact: Four open decisions have no named decision owner until the roles are confirmed.

text: REQ-DRI-001 to 005 and 009 to 012 belong to P7 rwb-decision, and REQ-DRI-006 to 008 and 013 to P2 rwb-integration.
why: The prefix is shared by two sections, and the section a requirement is written under is the only statement of the module that owns it.
read: A requirement ID of the form REQ-DRI alone does not identify the delivering service; the section does.
impact: Wrong split puts the decision log and the outbound adapters in the same service epic.

text: REQ-ILG-001 to REQ-ILG-014 are delivered by RWB-SVC-P1 rwb-source-data, although they are written in section 5.7.
why: The source precedence default ruling and DP-18 give the interaction ledger to P1, and the Ownership Map rules the interaction table to P1.
read: The case timeline and the interaction API stay with P3; the ledger itself and its intake rule are P1's.
impact: Otherwise the ledger is built twice, once in P3 and once in P1.

text: REQ-APD-001 to REQ-APD-011 are delivered by RWB-SVC-P7 rwb-decision, and the delegation of authority table they read belongs to P4 rwb-access.
why: The approvals are written under P7 and the Ownership Map rules the delegation table to P4.
read: P7 requests the limits from P4 through its contract; P4 holds the table and its versions.
impact: A single approval path depends on two service contracts; both must be in the same wave.

text: REQ-DRI-010 and REQ-DRI-011, the parameter catalog and the reference data service, are delivered by RWB-SVC-P3 rwb-case.
why: The source precedence default ruling gives parameters and reference data to P3, and the Ownership Map Parameters sheet records P3.
read: The rows stay written in section 5.7 so that the IDs remain stable.
impact: Every service that loads rules or thresholds depends on P3's contract.

text: Every release date is copied unchanged and marked tentative.
why: The programme dates are not yet fixed and a date is never raised as a gap.
read: 30 Nov 2026, 31 Dec 2026, 31 Jan 2027, 28 Feb 2027, 31 Mar 2027, 30 Apr 2027, 31 May 2027 and 30 Jun 2027, each marked tentative.
impact: A reader may plan to the dates, so the tentative mark must not be dropped downstream.

text: The business epic of a requirement is the Epic column of its own table in section 5, read from E1 to E8 as EP01 to EP08.
why: Section 5 states the release epic of every requirement and nothing else in the document does.
read: A requirement with E2 in its Epic column lands in EP02 and in the 31 Dec 2026 release.
impact: The release plan and the trace table disagree if a requirement is re-scoped without updating its Epic column.

text: P8 payment, P9 reporting and P10 agent have no requirement section in this BRD, and their service epics appear in the delivery model with no requirement row.
why: Section 5 has sixteen sections and names no P8, P9 or P10 section.
read: Their duties are stated inside other sections and are delivered by their own service epics in the wave the service is created.
impact: A traceability review may report three services with no business requirement; the service PRD is the answer.

text: The 78 non-functional requirements are delivered as non-functional work under RWB-ITG-NFR and the platform epics, not as rows of the business trace table.
why: Section 6 is a separate requirement set from the 231 business requirements, and the realignment gives non-functional work its own epic.
read: Wave 0 carries the mechanism; the measured target is proven at the wave whose release first depends on it.
impact: No non-functional target is owned by a service epic, so the integration harness must carry them.
